title: Cohort-weighted surge shedder with ephemeral recovery unwind (hotfix)
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: During a recent regional spike we observed cohorts with bursty traffic remaining in a degraded state for extended periods due to a conservative reopen algorithm and uniform penalty decay. This PR introduces a cohort-weighted shedding policy that: (1) computes tenant cohort weights from recent request distributions, (2) applies proportional shed probabilities rather than hard cuts, and (3) adds an ephemeral recovery unwind path that allows small successful probes to accelerate a cohort's penalty decay. The change is intentionally conservative by default (feature-flag gated) and aims to reduce both tail latency and prolonged tenant starvation during soft failures.

Implementation summary:
- New coordinator: services/serving/shedder/cohort_controller.go implements a sliding-window cohort weight estimator and exposes an API to query a cohort's effective shed probability.
- Shedder logic: services/serving/shedder/probabilistic_shedder.go applies weighted probabilistic drops and consults the ephemeral_recovery manager before applying long-term penalties.
- Recovery manager: services/serving/shedder/ephemeral_recovery.go keeps short-lived probe state and allows fast unwind on verified light traffic.
- Metrics & telemetry: ops/telemetry/metrics.yaml adds cohort_priority_ratio, cohort_probe_success_rate and shed_decision_reasons.
- Config and feature flag: deployments/helm/values.yaml adds featureFlags.cohortWeightedShedding and default thresholds.
- Tests: services/serving/shedder/cohort_controller_test.go and integration/region_failover_cohort_test.go cover expected behavior under synthetic bursts and recovery scenarios.

Rollout & safety: feature-flag disabled by default. If enabled, the default policy enforces a maximum shed of 50% per cohort; SLO enforcer still has final veto.

Hotfix rationale: a small production incident where a single tenant cohort remained in soft-quarantine for hours motivated a fast, backwards-compatible fix that reduces dwell time while preserving fairness.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration test (regional simulation)
- [x] Telemetry added
- [x] Feature flag guarded
- [x] Dev review and canary run notes included

release_notes: Hotfix: Introduce cohort-weighted probabilistic shedding with ephemeral recovery unwind. Feature-gated and off by default. Reduces long-lived cohort quarantine dwell and improves tail latency under bursty tenant traffic.
review_comments: Marco Liu: Can you clarify how cohort weights are computed across region boundaries? We should ensure a regional failover won't reset weights unexpectedly.

Priya Menon: We persist only short window aggregates per-region; during failover we either rehydrate from the target region's recent window or fall back to global uniform weights. Added comments and a small integration test to cover this (region_failover_cohort_test).
Aisha Patel: Please add an explicit cap on maximum shed probability at runtime to avoid a misconfigured input causing >100% drops.
Priya Menon: Added runtime cap and validation in helm values; added a unit test for validation.
Jamal Carter: Verified metrics look sane in canary run. Approving pending small doc tweak.
Priya Menon: Updated release notes and added a note on enabling the feature flag during canary procedures.
discussion_summary: Reviewers requested regional boundary clarification and a runtime cap; both addressed. Canaries ran with no SLA regressions and metrics showed reduced cohort dwell. CI green; merged via squash. Ops to coordinate controlled enablement behind feature flag for next canary wave.
notes_for_ops: Enable featureFlags.cohortWeightedShedding=false in prod by default. For canary: toggle on in a single region for a limited tenant cohort set using helm override values. Monitor ops/telemetry#cohort_probe_success_rate and ops/telemetry#cohort_priority_ratio. Rollback: set feature flag to false and the system will resume legacy behavior immediately.
